'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]], [[Taliban insurgency]]
**[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
***The [[Taliban]] captures the [[border town]] of [[Islam Qala]], [[Herat Province|Herat]], [[Afghanistan]]'s biggest [[Afghanistan–Iran border|border crossing]] with [[Iran]]. [https://apnews.com/article/joe-biden-taliban-middle-east-iran-58629a955d5b1703f2536efc122ef171 (Associated Press)] [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/afghan-taliban-say-capture-key-border-crossing-with-iran/articleshow/84260040.cms (India Times)]
***A spokesperson for the Taliban says that they now control "85% of the territory" as the [[Afghan government]] vows to retake all seized districts. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20210709-taliban-says-it-controls-85-percent-of-afghan-territory-made-no-ceasefire-promise-to-us (France 24)]
***Taliban insurgents capture the border town of [[Torghundi]] on the [[Afghanistan–Turkmenistan border|border]] with [[Turkmenistan]] as the [[Afghan National Security Forces]] collapse in [[Herat Province|Herat]]. The [[Ministry of Interior Affairs (Afghanistan)|Ministry of Interior Affairs]] says that troops had been "temporarily relocated" and that efforts are underway to recapture the border crossing. [https://www.trtworld.com/asia/kabul-scrambles-as-taliban-seizes-turkmenistan-iran-border-crossings-48227 (TRT World)]
***A spokesperson for [[Kandahar Province]] Governor Rohullah Khanzada says that the Taliban has captured the city of [[Kandahar]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/07/09/world/asia/taliban-kandahar-afghanistan.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[China]] evacuates 210 nationals from Afghanistan on a flight to [[Wuhan]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/china-evacuates-210-nationals-from-afghanistan-amid-us-troops-pullout-101625814627798.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
*[[Assassination of Jovenel Moïse]]
**The [[Government of Colombia]] reports that 13 of the 26 Colombian mercenaries who killed [[Haiti]]an President [[Jovenel Moïse]] were retired members of the [[National Army of Colombia]]. Two were killed during the gunfight with the police while the eleven others were arrested. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/07/09/world/colombia-soldiers-suspects.html (''The New York Times'')]
**The [[Government of Haiti]] requests security and investigative assistance from the [[United States]]. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/562349-haiti-requests-us-security-forces-to-guard-infrastructure-amid-turmoil (''The Hill'')]
*[[Operation Barkhane]]
**[[President of France|French President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] announces that he will reduce the presence of [[French Armed Forces|troops]] in the [[Sahel]] to between 2,500 and 3,000 over the long-term, and will also close bases in [[Timbuktu]], [[Tessalit]] and [[Kidal]] in northern [[Mali]], as part of a reorganization effort to focus on missions in the Malian, [[Niger]]ien, and [[Burkina Faso|Burkinese]] border regions. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/9/france-to-pull-more-than-2000-troops-from-africas-sahel (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**More than 370 [[Palestinians]] are injured after Israeli security forces opened fire on demonstrators protesting the presence of an [[Evyatar|illegal outpost]] near [[Beita, Nablus|Beita]] in the occupied [[West Bank]]. Thirty-one of those injured were hit with live ammunition. Dozens more are injured in similar confrontations in [[Kafr Qaddum]], [[Beit Dajan, Nablus|Beit Dajan]], and [[Hebron]], with demonstrators in Hebron protesting the presence of [[Israeli settlement|settlements]] in the [[Masafer Yatta]] area. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/9/israel-forces-open-fire-on-palestinians-hundreds-wounded (Al Jazeera)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Lebanese liquidity crisis]]
**[[Lebanon]]'s electricity utility [[Électricité du Liban]] shuts down two of its biggest [[power station]]s due to lack of fuel, reducing total electrical output by 40% and leaving much of the country without power. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-57780940 (BBC News)]
*[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] [[List of executive actions by Joe Biden|signs]] a 72-point [[executive order]] placing tighter regulations and scrutiny on major corporations in a variety of sectors, including [[Big Tech]] companies. Policies outlined include banning [[non-compete clause]]s, curbing the ability of manufacturers to restrict the [[Electronics right to repair|right to repair certain products]], granting the [[Federal Trade Commission]] the ability to set guidelines on data collection, banning unfair competition practices in online marketplaces, and ordering the [[Food and Drug Administration]] to work with [[U.S. state|states]] and [[Tribe (Native American)|Native American tribal governments]] on procuring cheaper medicines from [[Canada]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-57783824 (BBC News)] [https://www.ft.com/content/c207e1c4-8978-4482-8b4d-c353acce33d1 (''FT'')] [https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/presidential-actions/2021/07/09/executive-order-on-promoting-competition-in-the-american-economy/ (WH.gov)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Atami landslide]]
**The death toll from the landslide in [[Atami]], [[Japan]], increases to nine, as more bodies are found under the mud. Twenty-two people are still missing. [https://jen.jiji.com/jc/eng?g=eco&k=2021070801237 (Jiji Press)]
*[[Surfside condominium building collapse]]
**The death toll in the [[Champlain Towers South]] [[condominium]] building collapse in [[Surfside, Florida|Surfside]], [[Florida]], increases to 78, with the overnight recovery of 14 more bodies. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/surfside-building-collapse-latest-death-toll-rises-60/story?id=78727253 (ABC News)]
*An airplane carrying [[Parachuting|skydivers]] crashes in [[Örebro]], [[Sweden]], killing all nine people on board. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-57774490 (BBC News)]
*The [[Federal Agency for Forestry (Russia)|Russian Federal Forestry Agency]] reports that 160 [[wildfire]]s are currently burning an area covering {{convert|4400|km2|mi2}} in the [[Siberia]]n [[Republics of Russia|republic]] of [[Sakha Republic|Sakha]]. [https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-yakutia-wildfires-/31351434.html (RFE/RL)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
****[[Johannesburg]] [[Mayor of Johannesburg|mayor]] [[Geoff Makhubo]] dies from [[COVID-19]]-related complications, after being hospitalized for a week. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/9/johannesburg-mayor-geoff-makhubo-dies-of-covid-19 (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]]
****[[Tunisia]] reports a record 189 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 16,050. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-07/10/c_1310052866.htm (Xinhuanet)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record 212 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 16,004. The country also surpasses one million cases of the virus. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/bangladeshs-covid-19-cases-cross-1m-mark-amid-record-deaths/2299862 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]], [[Community Activities Restrictions Enforcement]]
****The [[Government of Indonesia]] announces an extension of emergency community restrictions to 15 [[Regency (Indonesia)|regencies]] and [[City status in Indonesia|cities]] outside [[Java]] and [[Bali]] beginning on July 12 amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases outside Java and Bali. [https://amp.kontan.co.id/news/pemerintah-tetapkan-ppkm-darurat-di-15-kabupatenkota-di-luar-jawa-bali (Kontan)]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 28,975 recoveries in the past 24 hours, thereby surpassing the nationwide total of recoveries to 2 million. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5637470/dki-13112-kasus-ini-sebaran-38124-kasus-covid-19-ri-9-juli (detikHealth)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****The [[Israel]]i [[Ministry of Health (Israel)|Ministry of Health]] announces that all visitors who are traveling to Israel, including vaccinated individuals, will be required to quarantine for 24 hours or receive a negative [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 test]] beginning on July 16. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/friday-is-last-day-for-israelis-to-get-vaccinated-against-covid-before-doses-expire-1.9985339 (Haaretz)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 9,108 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 817,838. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/07/09/covid-19-malaysia-hits-new-daily-record-with-9-180-new-cases (''The Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]]
****[[Saudi Arabia]] approves the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccine]] developed by [[Moderna]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/amp/coronavirus/2021/07/09/Saudi-Arabia-approves-Moderna-COVID-19-vaccine-for-use (Al Arabiya)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 1,316 new cases of COVID-19, prompting the [[Government of South Korea|government]] to raise its restrictions to the highest "Level 4" in the [[Seoul Capital Area]] for two weeks beginning on July 12. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/07/09/south-korea-raises-covid-restrictions-in-seoul-to-top-level.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Germany]] declares all of [[Spain]] as a COVID-19 risk area, which will require travellers to present a negative [[COVID-19 testing|test result]] in order to avoid [[quarantine]] beginning on July 11, due to the spread of the more contagious [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/coronavirus-germany-declares-spain-a-covid-risk-area/a-58216999 (DW)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malta]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Malta]] announces that beginning on July 14, they will become the first country in [[Europe]] to close their borders to unvaccinated travellers, only allowing those with a Maltese, British or European [[Immunity passport|vaccination certificate]] to enter following an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/malta-closes-borders-to-unvaccinated-travellers-01625844009 (''Barron's'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports 25,766 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of new cases since January 2 and thereby brings the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 5.73 million. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-reports-25766-new-covid-19-cases-726-deaths-2021-07-09/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cuba]]
****[[Cuba]]n health regulator CECMED approves the emergency use of the domestically-produced [[Abdala (vaccine)|Abdala]] vaccine, becoming the fifth [[COVID-19 vaccine]] to be approved in the country. Manufacturers last month claimed that the vaccine, which requires three doses, has a 92% effectiveness rate against the virus. This makes Cuba the first [[Caribbean]] and [[Latin America|Latin American]] country to successfully develop its own variation of the vaccine. [https://www.dw.com/en/covid-cuba-approves-emergency-use-of-own-abdala-vaccine/a-58222105 (DW)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
*****[[California]] will require [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|face masks]] in schools despite [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|CDC]] guidelines saying that vaccinated students are not required to wear a mask. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2021-07-09/masks-wont-necessarily-come-off-students-in-l-a-schools-despite-cdc-guidelines (''Los Angeles Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
***[[Fiji]] reports a record 860 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the national total of cases to 9,521. The [[Ministry of Health and Medical Services (Fiji)|Ministry of Health  and Medical Services]] also reports three deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the national death toll to 51. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/446577/fiji-covid-19-positive-cases-pass-800-three-more-deaths-confirmed-in-latest-update (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]], [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
***A [[University of Campinas]] study finds that the [[CoronaVac]] COVID-19 vaccine is less effective against the [[Lineage P.1]] [[SARS-CoV-2 Gamma variant|Gamma variant]], which originated in [[Brazil]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/sinovac-covid-19-vaccine-less-effective-against-gamma-variant-15184826 (CNA)]
*[[Climate change in Australia]]
**[[government of Australia|Australia]]n [[Minister for the Environment (Australia)|Minister for the Environment]] [[Sussan Ley]] announces that she will appeal a historic ruling from the [[Federal Court of Australia|Federal Court]] which found that she has a "duty to take reasonable care" that young people will not be harmed in the future by the effects of [[global warming]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/jul/09/australian-government-to-appeal-ruling-that-it-must-protect-children-from-climate-harm (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Belarus–Lithuania relations]], [[European migrant crisis]]
**[[Lithuania]] begins construction on a $48 million [[Border barrier|fence]] along its border with neighboring [[Belarus]]. A week prior, Lithuania had declared a [[state of emergency]] due to an increase in the number of [[undocumented migrant]]s crossing into the country from Belarus, accusing Belarusian [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] of deliberately trying to destabilize the country by encouraging and allowing [[refugee]]s, mostly [[Syrians]], to illegally cross the border. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/lithuania-spending-2448m-to-erect-border-fence-with-belarus-to-stem-migration/ar-AALXS71?ocid=uxbndlbing (''Newsweek'')]
*[[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
**The Ukrainian [[Ministry of Defence (Ukraine)|Ministry of Defence]] accuses Russia of hacking the website of the [[Ukrainian Naval Forces]] to publish fake news and upload false documents regarding naval drills between Ukraine, [[NATO]], and most [[Black Sea]] nations. [https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-hack-russia-navy-sea-breeze/31351045.html (RFE/RL)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Murder of Sarah Everard]]
**[[Metropolitan Police|London police officer]] Wayne Couzens pleads guilty to the [[murder in English law|murder]] of Sarah Everard. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-57774597 (BBC News)] 

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[South Sudanese Civil War]]
**[[President of South Sudan|President]] [[Salva Kiir Mayardit]] promises peace on Independence Day and also offers peace to opponent [[Riek Machar]]. A [[civil war]] has been fought in [[South Sudan]] since 2013 when ethnic differences contributed to an armed conflict that has killed more than 400,000 people. This offer of peace comes after [[Pope Francis]] said that he would visit the Christian-majority country if some kind of peace is achieved. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/independence-day-south-sudans-kiir-pledges-no-more-war-pope-says-will-visit-2021-07-09/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Dublin Bay South by-election]]
**In Ireland, [[Labour Party (Ireland)|Labour]] candidate [[Ivana Bacik]] is declared the winner in a [[by-election]] for the [[Dublin Bay South (Dáil constituency)|Dublin Bay South]] constituency, wresting control from the ruling [[Fine Gael]]. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/politics/bacik-over-the-moon-as-she-wins-dublin-bay-south-byelection-1.4615698 (''The Irish Times'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*The [[Ministry of Ecology and Environment|Chinese Ministry of Ecology and Environment]]'s Department of Nature and Ecology Conservation announces that it no longer considers the [[giant panda]] to be endangered, but instead considers it to be [[Vulnerable species|vulnerable]]. This comes five years after the [[International Union for Conservation of Nature]] made a similar reclassification. [https://theguardian.com/world/2021/jul/09/giant-pandas-no-longer-endangered-in-the-wild-china-announces (''The Guardian'')]
